subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is meant by the genome of an organism?
options: The entire genetic material of an organism
A single gene that controls one characteristic
The proteins made by a cell
The number of chromosomes in a gamete
questions.explain: The genome is the whole of the genetic material (all the DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: A gene is best described as:
options: A short section of DNA that codes for a particular protein
A complete strand of a chromosome
A molecule of glucose used for energy
questions.explain: A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a specific sequence of amino acids, and therefore a particular protein.

questions.q: In a DNA molecule, the base adenine (A) always pairs with which base?
questions.explain: Complementary base pairing means adenine pairs with thymine, and cytosine pairs with guanine.

questions.q: What is the shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.explain: DNA is made of two strands coiled together to form a double helix.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between DNA, genes and chromosomes?
options: A chromosome is a long molecule of DNA that carries many genes
A gene is made of many chromosomes joined together
DNA is made of many chromosomes
A chromosome codes for a single protein
questions.explain: Chromosomes are long DNA molecules, and each carries many genes along its length.

questions.q: What is an allele?
options: A different version of a gene
questions.explain: Alleles are alternative forms of the same gene found at the same position on a chromosome.

questions.q: An organism that has two identical alleles for a characteristic is described as:
questions.explain: Two identical alleles for a gene is a homozygous genotype; two different alleles is heterozygous.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a phenotype rather than a genotype?
questions.explain: The phenotype is the physical characteristic expressed, whereas the genotype describes the alleles present.

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a human male?
questions.explain: Human males have the sex chromosomes XY, while females have XX.

questions.q: Two heterozygous plants (Tt x Tt) are crossed. What is the expected ratio of tall to short offspring, where T (tall) is dominant?
questions.explain: A cross of Tt x Tt gives genotypes TT, Tt, Tt, tt, producing a 3:1 phenotype ratio.

questions.q: A heterozygous organism (Aa) is crossed with a homozygous recessive organism (aa). What proportion of offspring are expected to show the recessive characteristic?
questions.explain: Aa x aa produces Aa, Aa, aa, aa, so half the offspring are aa and show the recessive characteristic.

questions.q: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele. If both parents are carriers (heterozygous), what is the probability that a child will have cystic fibrosis?
questions.explain: Two carriers (Ff x Ff) have a 1 in 4 chance of producing an affected homozygous recessive (ff) child.

questions.q: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explain: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection.

questions.q: In which year did Charles Darwin publish 'On the Origin of Species'?
questions.explain: Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of variation caused only by the environment?
options: A scar caused by an accident
questions.explain: A scar is caused by the environment, whereas features such as blood group and eye colour are determined by genes.

questions.q: The formation of a new species is known as:
questions.explain: Speciation is the formation of a new species, often when populations can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

questions.q: Why do populations of antibiotic-resistant bacteria develop over time?
options: A mutation makes some bacteria resistant and these survive to reproduce
Bacteria choose to become resistant when exposed to antibiotics
Antibiotics turn bacteria into new resistant species
All bacteria are naturally resistant to antibiotics
questions.explain: Random mutations give some bacteria resistance; these survive the antibiotic and pass on the resistance allele through natural selection.

questions.q: What is selective breeding?
options: Choosing organisms with desired characteristics to breed together
Changing an organism's genes in a laboratory
Cloning an organism to make identical copies
Allowing organisms to breed at random
questions.explain: Selective breeding involves choosing parents with desirable characteristics and breeding them over generations.

questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of selective breeding and inbreeding in a population?
options: It reduces genetic variation and can increase inherited disease
It increases genetic variation too quickly
It removes all mutations from the population
questions.explain: Repeated inbreeding reduces genetic variation, making the population more vulnerable to inherited diseases and new conditions.

questions.q: Human insulin used to treat diabetes is now commonly produced using:
questions.explain: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria by genetic engineering so they produce human insulin.
